candidate.inputs: (left,right): finite acyclic *ground* first-order trees with UTF-8 symbolic atom or exact integer leaves and immutable functor/arity nodes
candidate.outputs: (most-specific generalization pattern G, left witness sigma1, right witness sigma2) with G sigma1=left, G sigma2=right; variables G0,G1,... canonical preorder; repeated ordered disagreement-pairs share one variable
candidate.behavior: Preserve identical subterms and equal functor/arity recursively. At a disagreement replace by a canonical variable keyed by the ordered pair of original subtrees. Same pair anywhere yields the same variable. Produce two exact reconstructions. No induction from uncertain observations, no side effects, no implicit backtracking.

positive_witnesses.why: same ordered mismatch pair uses ONE shared placeholder
different outer symbols generalize to variable
identical subterms retained; no gratuitous variable

falsifiers: UNIFY failure is not anti-unification failure: f(a) vs g(a) still yields fresh variable.
f(a,a) vs f(b,b) must NOT yield f(G0,G1): loses equality constraint and is less specific.
f(a,a) vs f(b,c) must NOT yield f(G0,G0): left instantiates but right cannot.
Changing a matching functor f/g child to fresh variable when symbols are equal yields needlessly general term.
All output witnesses must reconstruct both original terms exactly; no discarded substitutions.
No source aliases for native cyclic terms or pre-existing variables: those require separate law and runtime oracle.
Source supports cyclic term subsumption, but this proposed restricted input domain must explicitly reject cycles or non-ground terms.

dedup.difference: Unification finds a common INSTANCE (when possible) and may fail; anti-unification finds a most-specific common GENERALIZATION (always for valid ground inputs). Two witness substitutions and pair-sharing constraints distinguish the observable result.
dedup.derivable_warning: Can be programmed recursively from D3/D5/D9 term constructors, equality and environment maps; explicit Core-D10 primitive versus Core-Math/logic-library ownership has NOT been proved.
